note: The Principality of Galicia-Volhynia, after its 1241 Mongol devastation, became a tribute-paying vassal of the Golden Horde under Daniel of Galicia. Daniel alternated between accommodation (accepting the Horde's patent) and resistance (seeking crusade support from Pope Innocent IV, receiving a royal crown in 1253). The Horde used Galician troops in its western campaigns; Galician princes periodically made the journey to Sarai to renew their submission. After Daniel's line ended (1323), Galicia passed to Poland and Volhynia to Lithuania — both of which were rising powers outside the Horde's sphere, ending the tributary relationship.

_quarry.structural_significance: Galicia-Volhynia's tributary relationship with the Horde is the western fringe of the Mongol tributary system; Daniel's simultaneous papal crown and Horde tribute demonstrates the impossible diplomatic position of small states between great powers; the absorption by Poland and Lithuania ends the Horde's westernmost tributary sphere
